title: Backtesting and evaluation
summary: Compare resource forecasts with actual use and understand scores and rankings.
text: Rolling backtests Move forecast origins forward through time. Each run uses only history available before that origin, including all additional input metrics. Match windows and horizons to actual operating decisions. Read resource prediction performance Accuracy concerns resources such as CPU, memory, and GPU. Replica counts are derived from resource demand and constraints; distinguish them from actual and Ready replicas. Measure Meaning and use WAPE Total absolute error relative to total absolute actual values over the same window. Peak underestimation The risk of predicting less than actual high-water demand. Resource accuracy and score Read resource performance, completeness, and protection factors together. Scores do not override execution bounds. Actual evaluation Link observations to predictions after their target times arrive. Scores, rankings, and consensus The rankings page shows current performance and historical changes. Rank helps compare candidates; look-ahead decisions combine available forecasts and confidence rather than simply following the top-ranked method. Inspect training and run details for window, version, parameters, duration, and reasons. Recheck performance after configuration changes. Wait for actuals and keep evaluating Future target times do not yet have actual observations; missing evaluations are not zero error. Continue reviewing resource behavior and outcomes as inputs and workload patterns change. Read a module effect report Select a module and time window in forecasting results to review resource error, peak underestimation, scale-up timeliness, excess and missing capacity, reversals, degradation reasons, and algorithm adoption. Insufficient or unmeasurable data is identified rather than treated as zero error. Actual Pod-hours and capacity SLO The execution and capacity section compares observed Ready replicas with replicas required by measured load. It reports actual, needed, excess, and missing Pod-hours and minutes of insufficient capacity. Data gaps are excluded from compared time. Capacity SLO is time without a capacity shortfall divided by compared time. Its default target is 99%, configured with forecast.slo_capacity_target_percent . It is not a latency or error-rate SLO; excess Pod-hours are not proven monetary savings. Values require at least 12 compared moments covering at least half the requested window. Preview configuration changes Open change preview from the effect report to compare saved and proposed settings on the same history. Review shortfall and surplus windows, risk error, replica-hours, changes, and the largest differences. Compare methods and parameters, safety margin, per-Pod capacity, replica bounds, and short-term correction. Preview is read-only: it saves no recommendations, changes no modules, and performs no scaling. It compares forecast-derived replicas without fully replaying cooldowns, steps, look-ahead, or safeguards. Model services use pretrained models rather than background-tuned copies. Interpret results within this scope.

title: Recommendations and look-ahead
summary: Learn how model consensus, lead time, and constraints shape resource advice.
text: Read a recommendation snapshot A snapshot records resource advice, desired replicas, decisive factors, sources, version, and expiry. It explains what to configure and why; execution records show what was actually applied. Allow time for capacity to become ready Scaling only when demand arrives may be too late. Look-ahead decisions account for collection, prediction, control loops, Pod readiness, and node preparation where needed, then evaluate the corresponding future window. Scale-up and scale-down use different perspectives. Reductions require caution across future demand, live load, and readiness rather than reacting to a brief dip. Multi-model consensus Available candidates participate in the look-ahead window. Confidence combines scores with recent tracking error. A configured weighted quantile combines predictions before live load and safeguards settle the decision. Read consensus alongside the final replica count, constraints, and actual use. Without eligible predictions, use schedules, fallback, or unchanged values according to module rules. Resource and replica constraints CPU, memory, throughput, or JVM pressure may be decisive. Replica changes respect minimums, maximums, hard ceilings, steps, and cooldowns. OOM floors and memory peaks provide protection beyond smoothed point forecasts. Configured or estimated per-Pod capacity needs comparison with workload load tests. Advice, writes, and readiness are separate stages A submitted replica change does not mean the new Pods are Ready. Inspect actual replicas, readiness, and subsequent resource behavior. Forecast far enough for capacity to arrive For modules planning replica scaling, the effective horizon accounts for the module horizon, run interval, and readiness lead time. Default lead-time coverage is twice the lead time, capped at 24 hours, with the reason shown in recommendation details. Once enough scale-up outcomes exist, lead time uses measured readiness for that module and allows for recent late arrivals. Candidates that substantially lag recent actuals are excluded from consensus when healthy alternatives exist. Configurable emergency scale-up can cover observed demand above both forecasts and current capacity. This path only scales up and still respects replica ceilings.

title: Admission and scaling
summary: Enable Pod resource advice and replica scaling separately, then review outcomes.
text: Let the Operator adjust replicas Configure the target workload, replica bounds, step limits, and cooldowns. Auto requires authorization at both module and global levels before the Operator applies valid advice. Manage everything on the platform modules: the operator reads them and writes the replicas, and creates no resource of its own in the cluster. A target has exactly one replica owner. One replica owner per target Do not let the Operator, HPA, KEDA, or duplicate scalers write the same workload. Stop the previous controller and release ownership before reviewing the new controller in Observe. Apply resource advice to new Pods Admission reads the latest valid recommendation and adjusts CPU / memory requests and configured limits on new Pods. Unavailable advice should preserve original resources and allow deployment. New recommendations do not immediately change running Pods. Apply settings through creation or rolling updates. Assess and authorize memory-limit reductions separately. Review actual outcomes Inspect scaling and admission details for advice, applied results, and pause or failure reasons. Check current and Ready replicas, workload demand, and resource use to distinguish a submitted change from ready capacity. Did capacity arrive before demand? Open Expansion timeliness from scale-up records to inspect timely rate, late-arrival P90, emergency share, peak-underestimation P90, horizon-to-lead ratio, and decision wait. Each measure includes sample counts and status. Insufficient samples remain pending; suitable settings alone do not establish successful scale-up outcomes. Upward decisions are evaluated against subsequent demand and Ready replicas as timely, late, or demand not arriving. Evaluated readiness and lateness feed later lead times. This outcome assessment covers scale-ups rather than scale-downs. Report actions after an outage The Operator queues reports before sending and replays them in occurrence order after recovery. --report-spool-file persists them to a mounted file. Deployment manifests use emptyDir, surviving container restarts within the same Pod, not necessarily Pod replacement. The queue holds 10,000 records; overflow drops the oldest and increments a counter. Explicitly rejected records are removed so they do not block later reports. This is bounded delivery storage, not indefinite audit retention. Optional action columns include record_id , occurrence and reporting times, decision source, outage state, and Operator identity. The platform deduplicates by record ID and archives late reports by occurrence time. Requests, limit ratios, and OOM floors When configured, limit ratios apply to the final request: a 10 GiB memory request with a 1.2 ratio produces a 12 GiB limit. OOM uplift raises the request floor without repeatedly compounding the limit ratio. Admission calls carry request_uid and operation for attribution and deduplication. Queries without a request UID still return advice but do not create admission records.

title: Safety and fallback
summary: Manage schedules, fallback, bypass, and safeguards for automatic actions.
text: Modes and authorization Observe and Recommend help build an understanding of workload behavior. Admission and automatic scaling require both global authorization and a suitable module mode. Writes are disabled by default. Scheduled overrides Set fixed resources or replicas for defined business windows, including start, end, timezone, priority, and covered fields. Other fields follow their normal policies; normal calculation resumes after the window. Schedules use explicit IANA timezones and storage stays in UTC. The platform defaults to UTC+8 and pages display UTC+8. Never write converted display times back as storage values. Degradation and recovery Each field follows bypass → schedule → eligible model → module fallback → unchanged. Values must remain valid, fresh, and within bounds. OOM floors apply outside bypass. Record reasons for insufficient history, stale inputs, model failure, or missing eligible forecasts. Consecutive healthy cycles are required before recovery to avoid unstable switching. When manual intervention is needed Enable Bypass and record a reason. Disable the corresponding global setting and return to Recommend or Observe. Review snapshots, action records, and actual resources. Fix inputs or policy and compare results before gradually restoring authorization. Stopping future actions does not undo previous changes Bypass and global settings do not restore earlier resource or replica configurations automatically. Consider current service state and action history when restoring them. Configure OOM memory protection separately Modules separate OOM protection from prediction metrics. Configure lookback, memory uplift, and heap pressure, then connect OOM counts, pre-OOM working set, memory limits, and JVM heap metrics. Rules missing their required inputs do not apply, and recommendation details identify the missing inputs. OOM score weighting is disabled by default. When enabled, it penalizes memory scores only where memory was underallocated in the evaluation window; CPU scores are unaffected. Memory floors provide protection while scores compare models. Hold, degrade, and recover during an outage The Operator tracks each module separately. A connection fault does not immediately switch replicas to fallback. Configure timing in system settings; the platform distributes it. The following describes defaults. State Replica behavior Normal Follow platform decisions within module bounds, cooldowns, and steps. Cached Use a decision less than ten minutes old for scale-up only, without retaining urgency. Holding Without valid cache, retain current replicas for five minutes without immediately applying fallback. Degraded After the hold, move toward fallback in steps, only upward, with degradation cooldown between actions. Recovering Follow upward decisions; scale-down requires both two consecutive successful responses and at least five minutes of stable recovery. Configure decision and module cache lifetimes, hold, fallback cooldown, recovery responses, and stability through operator.decision_cache_ttl_seconds , module_cache_ttl_seconds , degrade_hold_seconds , degrade_cooldown_seconds , recover_answers , and recover_stable_seconds , all under the operator. prefix. Expired module configuration also holds replicas. An explicit no-decision answer outranks cached advice. The decision cache is in memory and does not survive restarts. Offline action reports can be persisted separately; see offline reporting .

title: AI assistant and skills
summary: Query platform state, use slash commands, export reports, and explain changes.
text: Open the AI assistant Enable assistant.enabled in system settings and grant the user assistant:chat . The assistant opens from the top-right button in a floating window. Turning off the global switch hides both the entry and the window. Manage connections and skills under AI configuration. Ask which modules need attention, whether a service scaled in time, or what the Operator did during an outage. The assistant reads stored modules, effect reports, scaling actions, and admission records as needed to answer. Use slash commands Type / to list available skills. Use the arrow keys to select, Enter to run, Tab to complete, and Esc to dismiss. Disabled skills are omitted. Command Purpose Requires an LLM /help List skills and argument requirements. No /report Produce a 24-hour usage report with document and JSON downloads. No /export Export the last 24 hours of service status. No /tasks List your AI scheduled tasks, next runs, and recent results. No /attention Explain modules needing attention. Yes /outage Review outages, queued reports, and degradation. Yes /actions [module] Explain scaling actions, optionally for a module. Yes /effect <module> Explain a module's forecasting effectiveness. Yes; module required /admission Explain admission records. Yes Reports and exports are built directly from stored facts and work without an LLM connection. The global switch and access permissions still apply. Manage and write skills Use AI configuration → Skill management. Built-in skills can be enabled or disabled; their prompts are read-only and they cannot be deleted. Model-dependent skills can select an LLM; otherwise they use the default. Custom skills define a command, title, description, argument mode (none, required, or optional), model, and prompt. Reference the argument using {{args}} . For example, create /review with a required module argument: Text Copy Analyze the last 24 hours of forecasts and scaling actions for module {{args}}. Separate recorded facts, possible causes, and missing information. Save and enable the skill to make it available in chat. Its selected model must be available; a skill without one follows the default connection. Data scope and actions The assistant queries existing records and does not change algorithm parameters, workload resources, or replicas. Forecasting remains with the forecasting methods, and execution remains with platform rules and the Operator. Read explanations alongside their underlying records. Chat can create, list, and delete the user's own AI scheduled tasks . These query the platform and send answers without resource changes. Tasks created through chat send only to the current user's own email. Chat, skills, and exports use assistant:chat . LLM, skill, and task management have separate permissions. Assistant access currently exposes platform-wide data, rather than an owner-only subset of modules. Troubleshooting Missing entry: check the global switch and chat permission. Reports work but questions fail: check the enabled default LLM, endpoint, model name, tool-calling compatibility, and credentials. Missing skill: check activation and supply required arguments. Incomplete answer: confirm that collection, recommendations, and execution records exist for the requested window.

title: LLM configuration
summary: Configure default and selected models, tools, advanced settings, and credentials.
text: Add a language model connection In AI configuration → LLM management, add a name, provider type, API base URL, model identifier, and credential. Test connection checks the current form. Include the provider's base prefix, such as /v1 , rather than a complete chat endpoint path. The current provider type uses the OpenAI-compatible protocol. Compatible gateways and self-hosted services can be configured; native Anthropic and Gemini protocols are not current provider types. Choose a model supporting tool calls to query platform data. Enabled, default, and selected models Multiple connections may be enabled. Ordinary questions, skills, and tasks without a selected model use the default connection; without an explicit default, the earliest enabled connection is used. A default connection must be enabled. Skills and tasks may select their own model. LLM management is for language models. Model management under forecasting connects time-series models such as Chronos for numerical forecasts; the two connection types are managed separately. Advanced settings Setting Purpose Request timeout Default 90 seconds, range 5–600, for one model request. Tool rounds Default 6, range 1–12, limiting successive tool-call rounds for a question. Temperature Optional sampling setting, subject to provider support. Maximum tokens Bounds a reply; zero omits the limit and lets the service decide. Context length Context budget; older messages are trimmed first. Zero means unknown and disables trimming by this setting. Proxy and TLS Configure a proxy or per-connection certificate-verification bypass. Retain verification for normal certificate connections. Custom headers Additional gateway headers, stored encrypted without returning saved plaintext. Custom JSON parameters Additional service parameters; model, messages, tools, stream, and other platform-managed fields cannot be overridden. Test connection uses the current endpoint, model, and advanced settings. Editing can reuse an existing credential. Save after testing and review the default selection. Credentials and permissions Credentials and custom header values are encrypted and are not returned in plaintext in lists or edit forms. Connection management and chat have separate permissions. System settings retain only the global assistant.enabled switch. Manage endpoints, credentials, and limits in LLM management. Explicit database migration moves legacy assistant parameters into connection records. After connecting Test the connection and verify the model identifier and credential. Enable it, select the default, and ask the assistant a question requiring platform data. Review tool reads and the answer to verify tool-call compatibility. Select other enabled models for skills or tasks with different needs.

title: AI scheduled tasks and email
summary: Ask on a schedule, retain answers, and deliver them by email.
text: Ask on a schedule and email the answer An AI scheduled task combines a prompt, schedule, recipients, answer language, and optional LLM. The platform asks the model at the scheduled time using the assistant's platform-query tools, stores the answer, and sends it by email. Examples include daily status summaries, weekly effectiveness reviews, and periodic degradation checks. Tasks do not modify resources or parameters. Results depend on the prompt, available records, and model. Scheduled questions do not replace continuous alert rules. Create a task Ask in chat: “Every Monday at 9, email me the usage status of all modules.” The assistant reports the schedule and next run. The current user must have an identity and valid email; chat-created tasks send only to that user's own address, regardless of other recipients in the prompt. Use /tasks to list your tasks. Administrators manage all tasks under AI configuration → Scheduled tasks, including prompts, schedules, recipients, language, activation, and models. They can run a task immediately and inspect each answer. Schedules and timezones Schedules use the platform timezone, UTC+8 by default. The examples below assume UTC+8. The minimum interval is one hour, each user may have 20 tasks, and prompts are limited to 2000 characters. Schedule Meaning 0 9 * * 1 Every Monday at 09:00. 0 8 * * * Every day at 08:00. 0 9 1 * * The first day of each month at 09:00. @every 24h A 24-hour interval, rather than a fixed daily clock time. Check the displayed next run before saving. Missed historical slots are not replayed individually: an overdue task runs once after recovery, then advances to a future slot. A task still running skips the next occurrence to avoid overlap. Configure email Configure SMTP in System management → System parameters, under notifications. Tasks send through the platform notification channel. Parameter Purpose notify.email.host / port SMTP server and port. notify.email.security starttls , tls , or none , matching the server. notify.email.username / password Login credentials; passwords are encrypted and masked. notify.email.from Sender address. notify.email.skip_verify Whether to bypass server certificate verification. notify.email.timeout_seconds Connection and delivery timeout. Password authentication is sent only over encrypted or local connections. Email is currently plain text with Markdown retained as text. Runs and retries Runs use the task center. Inspect answers, tools read, recipients, and delivery status. Retries reuse an existing answer rather than asking again, and recipients already sent successfully are not resent on a retry of the same job. For missing mail, check activation and next run, the selected or default model, task-center errors, SMTP, and recipient addresses. Configure missing models or email channels before retrying.

title: Dashboard and activity
summary: Review module status, attention flags, and applied scaling activity.
text: Review platform activity on the home page Users with home-page access land on the dashboard after login. A shared time window shows enabled and total modules, operating modes, modules needing attention, applied scaling actions, and failed runs. Modules needing attention Flag What to inspect Repeated failure At least three consecutive failures: inspect recent errors, sources, and model runs. Degraded recommendation Review sources and fallback reasons. Expired recommendation Check scheduling, forecasting, and decision refresh. No recommendation A module expected to produce advice has not done so; review module and metric settings. Bypass Confirm whether manual intervention is intentional. Observe-only modules and modules with prediction disabled are not flagged solely for missing advice. Bypass may be intentional; read its reason. Distinguish execution and effectiveness The dashboard reads existing state without starting forecasts, execution, or repairs. The scaling chart aggregates successfully applied Operator actions over time, not forecast recommendations. Empty periods show zero actions. Open Effect report from an attention row to inspect accuracy, timeliness, capacity, and stability.

title: Monitoring and troubleshooting
summary: Trace issues from data sources and model runs to actual replica readiness.
text: Troubleshoot along the workflow Symptom Check first No history Source, template variables, labels, time range, and units. Some models have no results Sample requirements, parameters, inputs, and runtime in model-run details. Evaluation is empty Whether target times have arrived and actuals have been collected. Fallback advice Snapshot sources, input freshness, eligibility, and recovery state. Replicas are unchanged Authorization, bypass, conflicts, expiry, step limits, and cooldowns. Desired count changed but capacity is low Current replicas, Ready status, Pod startup, and preparation time. Inspect metrics and curves Use the metric catalog and query tools to compare history, forecasts, actual performance, freshness, and runtime status. Distinguish missing samples from observations; connections across gaps are not measurements. External monitoring Set metrics.listen to expose /metrics , /healthz , and /readyz . Platform metrics use kube_res_foresight_* ; Operator metrics use kube_res_foresight_operator_* . Metrics observe the workflow rather than replacing snapshots, action reports, or readiness. Synchronous admission does not wait for long Prometheus queries or inference. Review connected records Follow a module through model runs, forecasts, evaluations, recommendations, admission, and scaling. For offline review, use audit exports with the appropriate scope and permissions. Watch decision sources and scaling delays Distinguish platform responses, cached decisions, recovery, and expired caches. Inspect kube_res_foresight_operator_decision_source_total and kube_res_foresight_operator_decision_cache_age_seconds , then correlate expansion timeliness with Ready-replica curves to separate forecast lag from slow capacity readiness. No model output is expected when prediction is disabled. Check the module's prediction mode before investigating data, models, and execution.

title: Administration
summary: Manage access, scheduled tasks, audit, and time settings.
text: Users, roles, and permissions Use user, role, menu, and API permissions to define access. Separate viewing results, editing policies, and authorizing execution. Grant machine credentials minimal permissions for their purpose. Directory authentication Configure LDAP under System → System parameters: connection, user and group queries, role mapping, checks, and synchronization. LDAPS / StartTLS settings are supported. Local accounts keep local authentication for emergency access. Tasks and global settings The task center manages schedules and execution records. Review inputs and errors before retrying. Global settings hold safety gates, look-ahead controls, and defaults; modules hold workload-specific policies and bounds. Storage and display time Store timestamps in UTC. The platform defaults to UTC+8, configurable through KUBE_RES_FORESIGHT_TIMEZONE for logs, database sessions, and new module schedules. Pages display UTC+8 regardless of browser timezone. Schedule intervals use explicit IANA timezones. Logs, retention, and export Login logs record authentication; operation logs track configuration and exports. Recommendation, execution, admission, and degradation records explain resource changes. Set retention for review needs and back up both the database and stable encryption key. Control history and admission record volume Set forecast.history_retention_days to override history retention; the default 0 keeps each record type's built-in period. forecast.evaluation_max_per_module keeps the latest 20,000 measured evaluations per module by default, with a minimum of 100. Admission calls need request_uid to create records, with deduplication by UID. With revision information, admission records creation and the first Pod of each new revision. Later scaling or replacement Pods are processed normally without individual records. Enable forecast.admission_record_scaling to include them. Calls with a UID but no revision information continue to be recorded individually. AI configuration and notifications assistant.enabled controls the chat entry. AI configuration manages LLM connections , skills , and scheduled tasks . Grant their menu permissions separately from assistant:chat . Email uses notify.email.* under notification settings. Check the model connection, user email, and SMTP; inspect task results through task records and the task center.

title: Common questions
summary: Find answers about setup, model choice, operating modes, and resource updates.
text: Can this website manage my cluster? This website provides project information and guides. Deploy the management platform separately to connect sources, configure modules, inspect advice, and authorize actions. Which model should I choose? Start with a baseline and compare resource error, peak underestimation, and runtime over the same history and horizon. Complexity does not replace workload performance. Available forecasts can also contribute to consensus. Can I use HPA or KEDA at the same time? They may manage other workloads, but must not control the same target replicas. Stop the old controller and release ownership before switching. Why are predictions or scores missing? First check whether prediction is enabled and whether No prediction is selected. New modules start with prediction disabled; configured fallback defaults are intentional. Then check sources, template labels, units, history, model runs, and freshness. Actual scores require the target time to arrive and matching observations to be collected. Do running Pods immediately receive updated advice? Admission affects new Pods; running configurations change through creation or rolling updates. Replica scaling is a separate action performed by the Operator. How do I pause automation? Enable module bypass or disable the corresponding global gate, then return to Observe or Recommend. Review actual resources before restoring earlier settings; bypass does not undo previous changes.
